errors.description: THE ABSENCE IS NOT DEMONSTRATED. This is an absence option - the subject is smoothness itself - and the render is a near-black charcoal cloth lit by a broad essentially frontal soft source. Across the whole hip and upper thigh field there is almost no tonal modelling and no specular sheen; the front panels read as flat dark shapes. A PLEATED front photographed under this same light on this same cloth would look very nearly identical, so the image carries no information distinguishing it from its neighbours on the pleat-style menu.
errors.expected: The drawing's whole point is that the front panels between the fly and the pockets are blank - an unbroken plane from waistband to thigh
errors.actual: A near-black front lit flat, where a smooth plane and a folded plane would be indistinguishable
errors.correction: Light the trouser front with a raking source from one side, low and near-grazing across the cloth, so the front panel resolves as one continuous unbroken plane with a smooth gradient from lit edge to shadow edge and a soft sheen travelling uninterrupted from the waistband to the thigh; choose a mid-tone cloth with visible weave so that continuity is legible.

errors.description: Front pocket openings. The drawing clearly shows a slant pocket mouth on each side, each drawn as a doubled line running from the waistband at (205,160) down to (135,545) on the left and (995,160) to (1065,545) on the right - a long near-vertical opening set in from the side seam. In the render no pocket mouth can be resolved on either hip; there are faint vertical tonal edges near x=120 and x=810 but nothing that reads as a defined opening.
errors.expected: A clearly defined slant front pocket opening on each side, running from the waistband seam down toward the hip
errors.actual: No legible pocket opening on either side; if present, it is lost in the dark cloth
errors.correction: Render a crisply pressed slant front pocket mouth on each hip, running from the waistband seam down and slightly outward toward the side seam, with a defined edge and a bar tack at the lower terminus, lit so the opening's edge separates from the surrounding panel.

errors.description: Ambiguous vertical folds high on both front panels. Two soft vertical fold lines run from close under the waistband down each front panel (left around x=240 descending from y=560, right around x=690 from y=570). In the drawing the front creases begin much lower - at y=690, which is 54 percent of the way from the waistband seam (y=155) to the frame bottom (y=1140). In the render the equivalent creases start at about 38 percent of that span. They read as pressed leg creases starting high rather than as pleats, but on an ABSENCE option a soft vertical fold running up under the waistband is exactly what a customer would misread as a pleat.
errors.expected: Front creases beginning at roughly mid-thigh, a bit past halfway down the panel, with the cloth above them completely uninterrupted
errors.actual: Soft vertical folds beginning close under the waistband on both panels, ambiguous between a high-starting crease and a soft pleat
errors.correction: Press the front crease so it begins only at mid-thigh, roughly halfway down the visible panel, and keep the cloth above it as one uninterrupted plane running clean from the waistband seam.

errors.description: Belt loop count and spacing. The drawing shows two loops in the front field, at x=380 and x=818 about a centre front of x=600 - symmetric at plus/minus 220. The render shows at least three, at x=285, x=618 and x=750 about a fly at x=460, so the loop at +290 has no counterpart at the mirrored position on the left.
errors.expected: Two front belt loops placed symmetrically either side of the fly
errors.actual: Three or more loops with the outermost one unmatched on the opposite side
errors.correction: Set two front belt loops, one either side of the fly at equal distance from centre front, with the next pair falling out toward the side seams beyond the frame.

errors.description: Fly topstitch run. The drawing's fly stitch drops from the waistband at y=155 to its curve at y=640, 49 percent of the waistband-to-frame-bottom span. The render's runs from about y=195 to y=520, about 34 percent of its equivalent span. Crops differ so this is approximate.
errors.expected: A fly topstitch running roughly half the visible panel depth before hooking toward centre
errors.actual: A shorter fly run, about a third of the panel depth
errors.correction: Run the fly topstitch down about half the visible depth of the front before curving in toward the centre-front seam, in a thread that sits close in tone to the cloth.

lockedFeatures: Front is genuinely flat - no pleat folds and no stitched darts anywhere on either front panel; the absence itself is respected
Waistband depth proportionally correct against the drawing
J-shaped fly topstitch present and correctly shaped
Left/right silhouette symmetric with a clean side-seam taper
Red bar-tack ticks in the drawing correctly read as documentation and not rendered as red thread
No numerals, arrows, leader lines or callouts traced into the photograph

do not change the garment part, orientation, or any other option's geometry

notes: The render DOES respect the absence: both panels between the fly and the pockets were checked and carry no pleat fold and no dart stitching. It fails on the second half of the absence test. On near-black cloth under flat frontal light there is essentially no surface modelling, so the image does not affirmatively SHOW flatness; it merely fails to show a pleat, which is not the same thing and leaves it indistinguishable from every neighbouring option. This is the documented failure mode for options whose only signal is depth - the remedy is raking light, exactly as it was for back-side-pleat. Compounding it, the drawn front pocket openings are not resolvable, and two soft vertical folds run high on both panels which, while most consistent with high-starting leg creases, are close enough to soft pleats to be misread on precisely the option where that misreading is fatal. Fabric weave was NOT measurable at this exposure.
